cenas.texto: In 1972, Honda took a big risk with a tiny car. The first Civic was small, simple, and incredibly efficient. And it changed how the world saw Japanese cars.
By the late eighties, the CR-X turned that efficiency into pure fun. Light, nimble, and made for twisting mountain roads.
Then, in 1990, came the NSX. A mid-engine supercar, fine-tuned with help from Ayrton Senna, proving Honda could take on Ferrari.
Today, the Civic Type R carries that spirit, with track-bred handling and a rear wing it wears with pride.
And the S2000? A roadster that revved to nine thousand R P M. Subscribe to Honda Deep Dive for the story behind every legend.
